projects.name: Eswatini Big Five Nature Reserve Project
projects.description: Ecotourism is an integral part of economic development and biodiversity conservation in the Kingdom of Eswatini and is largely based on nature reserves. The proposed Big Five Nature Reserve Project aims to integrate five large existing private and state nature reserves, cattle farms, and portions of communal lands under a single management structure in Eswatini. This is situated in the north-eastern part of the country in the Lubombo region and will entail merging 83,329.33 hectares of pristine land for conservation and tourism development. The reserve will establish recreational and leisure facilities including hiking trails, cultural heritage sites and aerial tours (hot air balloon, cable car), with tremendous job opportunities and increasing tourism. projects.name: Africa Minigrids Programme
projects.description:
The UNDP-supported, GEF-financed Africa Minigrids Program (AMP) aims to support African countries, including Eswatini, to increase energy access by reducing the cost and increasing commercial viability of renewable energy (RE) minigrids. 
For Eswatini, the AMP focus is on establishing a springboard for RE minigrid development, building data and knowledge resources and ‘proof of concept’ business models that can inform planning, de-risk investments and encourage private sector participation in the country. This aligns with the country targets for renewable energy (RE) and the expectation that minigrids will contribute to the goal to achieve universal energy access, as set out by the National Energy Policy (2018) and the Kingdom of Eswatini Energy Masterplan, 2034.
This contribution will be achieved through three outcomes: (i) appropriate policies and regulations addressing policy, institutional, regulatory and technical barriers to investment in RE minigrids; (ii) innovative business models, based on cost reduction, operationalized; and (iii) increased awareness and network opportunities in the minigrid market and among stakeholders as well as lessons learned for scaling up rural electrification using RE minigrids. 
The number of direct project beneficiaries is expected to be around 459 persons, of whom approximately 234 women. The lifetime global environmental benefits that will accrue from the adoption of clean energy minigrid technologies is estimated at 2,444 tCO2e. Indirect emission reductions amounting to 54,000 tCO2e are expected due to investments in minigrids completed during the 10-year influence period following project completion, predominantly through the replication of the sustainable technology value chain. The project yields a GEF abatement cost of 1,086 USD/tCO2e. This abatement cost takes into consideration overall upfront and replacement Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) of both pilots, as well as CAPEX for Productive Use of Energy (PUE) overlay.

projects.name: Increasing the resilience of Eswatini’s agropastoral communities through integrated ecosystems and watershed management
projects.description: This project seeks to increase the resilience of agropastoral communities living in the middle and lowveld regions of Eswatini, who are vulnerable to increases in temperature, drought and heavy rainfall related impacts, by promoting the sustainable management of ecosystems and watersheds. This will be achieved through ecosystem-based adaptation approaches, including sustainable approaches to conserving vegetation, maintaining soil fertility, reducing erosion, increasing the storage and supply of water for agriculture, developing/promoting sustainable agricultural value chains, unlocking public and private-sector finance, and establishing innovative funding mechanisms for sustainable agriculture and restoration. Together these approaches will improve agropastoral livelihoods/incomes, protect and restore biodiversity.
